# Dungka!

The name "Dungka!" refers to multiple distinct entities across different domains, including a prominent pop song by the Filipino group SB19, a contemporary lifestyle brand, and a niche candle-making company rooted in Buddhist tradition. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of each entity, detailing their respective origins, philosophies, cultural significance, and areas of operation. The analysis clarifies that these subjects, despite sharing a common name, exist independently with no known connection based on available sources. The primary focus is on the SB19 song, which has garnered significant attention in the realms of popular music and cultural studies, while also providing detailed profiles of the commercial and religious entities that share the same moniker.

## Dungka! (Song)

"Dungka!" is a high-octane pop track by the Filipino boy band SB19, released in Spring 2025 as part of their third extended play, *Simula at Wakas* , . It quickly emerged as a culturally resonant work, celebrated for its fusion of contemporary music trends with potent local language and imagery . Written solely by the group's leader, Pablo, and co-produced with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase, the song showcases the band's internal creative depth and their ability to craft a piece that is both globally accessible and deeply rooted in Filipino identity . Its release marked the second single from the EP, following "DAM" . The track's impact is defined by its defiant lyrical content, maximalist rave-fueled production, and a powerful message of self-expression and resilience that resonated strongly with audiences both within the Philippines and internationally , . The song's success is evidenced by its favorable critical reception and notable chart performance, solidifying its place as a significant cultural artifact in the Philippine pop landscape .

The conceptual core of the song lies in its linguistic construction and its use of Tagalog slang. The title "Dungka!" is a phonetic wordplay on the common Filipino phrase 'doon ka', which translates literally to 'go over there' or colloquially as an exhortation to 'go away' , . This phrase is used repeatedly throughout the lyrics to dismiss haters, negativity, and unwanted forces, transforming a simple directive into a playful, defiant refrain . Critics have described this refrain as functioning almost like a "winking incantation," a "gatekeeping spell" that requires cultural fluency to fully appreciate, serving to repel bad vibes and dead weight . This clever wordplay is a testament to Pablo's songwriting skills, as praised by reviewers who noted how he elevates a common expression into a powerful anthem . The symbolism extends beyond Tagalog, as the Hiligaynon language uses the word to mean "to arrive at port," adding another layer of meaning related to life journeys, movement, and resilience . This dual linguistic foundation allows the song to speak to a wide audience while retaining a unique cultural specificity that fuels its empowering message.

Musically, "Dungka!" is characterized as an "experimental banger" that embraces a maximalist production style, incorporating elements of rave and hyper-pop . The production, handled by Pablo and his brother Josue under their RadKidz moniker, was described by critics as "blaring [and] sharp" and the overall song as "irresistibly catchy" , . The composition features a "rave-fueled" pounding beat that drives the track forward with high energy . A key feature of the song is the dynamic exchange of bold rap verses between members Pablo and Josh, showcasing the group's lyrical prowess and contributing to the track's energetic and cutting edge . The final product is described as being both "jubilant and cutting," creating a unique sonic experience that invites revelry while simultaneously delivering a sharp, assertive message . This blend of infectious melody and aggressive lyricism makes the song a standout in SB19's discography and a compelling entry in the P-pop genre.

The song's themes are brought to vivid life in its six-minute music video, which serves as a rich tapestry of Filipino culture and social commentary . Directed by Kerbs Balagtas of YouMeUs MNL, the video was filmed in Manila’s urban streets and deliberately rejects Westernized aesthetics . Instead, it presents an unfiltered and authentic portrayal of everyday Filipino life, using real settings such as street courts, local eateries (*carinderias*) selling *kwek-kwek* and *isaw*, parking-lot Zumba sessions, and iconic jeepneys lit by the sunset , . This visual strategy frames the chaotic beauty of ordinary days in the Philippines as "vivid, messy, and magnetic," affirming local identity as "world-class" without filters , . The video's narrative is woven through scenes of community, celebration, and quiet defiance, challenging stereotypes and celebrating the spirit of resilience.

The music video incorporates layered symbolism and social critique. One prominent scene features Ghost Wrecker portraying "crab mentality," a satirical depiction of envy and negativity that the song seeks to dispel . Other scenes challenge traditional gender roles, such as those featuring Zumba dancing, and highlight Filipino street smarts and nonviolent expression through fliptop rap battles hosted by Shehyee and Smugglaz . The overarching message of the video is one of empowerment and perseverance: "Life is tough... but go live your life anyway. Wear what you want. Dance how you feel. Be whoever the heck you want to be" . This message is amplified by the inclusion of numerous cameos from other Filipino artists and public figures, transforming the narrative into a collective expression of resistance and celebration . These cameos include Vice Ganda strutting down the street, Mimiyuuuh drinking water mid-protest, Ben&Ben members joining a protest, Maymay Entrata dancing karaoke, Alodia Gosiengfiao teleporting from an arcade cabinet as a *Tekken*-inspired character, and many others, all embodying themes of collective action and resistance to flawed systems , .

Upon its release on April 25, 2025, "Dungka!" received favorable reviews from various media outlets. Billboard Philippines' Rome Saenz praised its blaring production and catchy nature, while Nylon Manila's Rafael Bautista and Preview's Kyla Villena labeled it as "loud" . The song achieved significant commercial success, peaking at #21 on the Philippines Hot 100 chart and reaching #7 on Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart during the week of May 10, 2025 . Its popularity was further demonstrated by the music video, which garnered one million views on YouTube within 24 hours of its release . Beyond its initial release, "Dungka!" has become integrated into the band's live performances and fan engagement. During a concert at the Bicol Music Festival, member Stell instructed fans to interact by staring at the person beside them and saying "Dungka!" to maintain distance, showcasing the song's cultural resonance and its adoption as a tool for communal activity . The song is scheduled as a key performance in SB19's Simula at Wakas World Tour, positioned after "I Want You" in the setlist to reignite intensity with plans for new outfits and staging inspired by the video's vibrant aesthetic .

## DUNGKA! (Contemporary Lifestyle Brand)

Founded by a team with extensive backgrounds in overseas market operations, product development, design, and art trend influence, the brand approaches its creations with a strategic and global perspective . In Himalayan Buddhism, the white conch is a sacred symbol imbued with profound meaning, representing the three thousand worlds and associated with Bodhidharma, the semi-mythical Buddhist monk traditionally credited with establishing Chan Buddhism . By adopting this ancient term, the brand establishes a strong and authentic spiritual lineage, positioning its products as vessels for tranquility and positive energy. This etymological choice grounds the brand in a rich cultural heritage, suggesting that its offerings are more than just material objects; they are imbued with a sense of history and sacredness.

Rather than relying on traditional Tibetan sign elements that might carry regional limitations, the brand consciously replaces them with a more universal aesthetic . This approach aims to transcend geographical and cultural boundaries, enabling the products to harmoniously integrate into diverse urban homes. The goal is to create a "new modern oriental tone" that respects the essence of Himalayan aesthetics while making it accessible and appealing to a contemporary, global audience . This design strategy reflects a careful balance between honoring its spiritual origins and embracing modern minimalism, ensuring that the products are both meaningful and stylish. The result is a collection that offers comfort and aesthetic pleasure, allowing individuals to bring a sense of peace and harmony into their living spaces .

All products, whether they are fragrances or home goods, are designed to serve a higher purpose than mere decoration or utility . They are intended to provide a source of comfort and relaxation, helping users to navigate the stresses of modern life. This holistic approach aligns with broader wellness trends but distinguishes itself through its specific and deliberate integration of Himalayan Buddhist symbolism and principles. The brand's emphasis on practicality and simplicity further reinforces this goal, advocating for a clutter-free and serene environment where one can find clarity and restorative energy .

In summary, the DUNGKA! lifestyle brand operates on a clear set of principles derived from its name's spiritual significance. It combines the wisdom of Himalayan Buddhism with a modern, minimalist design sensibility to create products that are both beautiful and functional. The brand's commitment to practicality, simplicity, and stability, coupled with its mission to infuse mental and spiritual energy, positions it as a provider of holistic well-being. Unlike the energetic and rebellious pop song, the DUNGKA! brand project is contemplative, focused on creating lasting serenity and a deeper connection to one's surroundings. The two entities, while sharing a name, represent vastly different worlds: one a vibrant expression of youth culture, the other a thoughtful pursuit of timeless tranquility.

SB19’s ‘DUNGKA!’ Is a Joyful Portrait of Filipino Life—And a Sharp Middle Finger To Negativity
==============================================================================================

In a luminous swirl of street life, protest chants, and sticky-sweet nostalgia, _DUNGKA!_ captures the defiant heartbeat of a nation refusing to stand still

By [Dayne Aduna](https://vman-sea.com/author/dayne-aduna/ "Posts by Dayne Aduna")

April 26, 2025

[![Image 4: Facebook](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/facebook?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F&linkname=SB19%E2%80%99s%20%26%238216%3BDUNGKA%21%26%238217%3B%20Is%20a%20Joyful%20Portrait%20of%20Filipino%20Life%E2%80%94And%20a%20Sharp%20Middle%20Finger%20To%20Negativity "Facebook")[![Image 5: Instagram](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/instagram.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Instagram")[![Image 6: X](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/x.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "X")[![Image 7: Email](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/email.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Email")[![Image 8: Copy Link](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Copy Link")

  ![Image 9: sb19 DUNGKA!](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/sb19-dungka-banner.webp?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

A soundtrack for defiance and joy
---------------------------------

It was only fitting that SB19—the luminary architects of P-pop’s current renaissance—graced the cover of our [Spring 2025 issue](https://vman-sea.com/on-the-cover/sb19-the-brotherhood-behind-the-music-and-why-theyre-stronger-than-ever/). Even then, they seemed poised on the brink of another breakthrough, and with the release of the _DUNGKA!_ music video, they have, once again, pushed beyond the expected.

_DUNGKA!_ is a six-minute exhale of Filipino life: vivid, messy, and magnetic. The music video stitches together a tapestry of the archipelago’s pulse—street basketball courts alive with sweaty, frenetic games; vendors hawking _kwek-kwek_ and _isaw_; karaoke sessions conducted in cracked plastic chairs; Zumba in parking lots; children hopping between chalk squares in 10-20; rally banners flapping against concrete and sky. Election campaigns roar in the background, as much a fixture of the landscape as the sunset-lit jeepneys rattling down narrow streets. Every frame hums with the particular, chaotic beauty of ordinary days in the Philippines.

And threaded through it all, like a live wire: SB19, effortless in their command, moving not above the scenes, but through them.

_ALSO READ: [FELIP’s Meteoric Rise](https://vman-sea.com/arts-culture/music/felips-meteoric-rise/)_

Staying stubbornly, brilliantly local
-------------------------------------

Musically, _DUNGKA!_— produced by Pablo and his brother Josue under their RadKidz moniker—is a rave-fueled masterstroke. Over a pounding beat, Pablo and Josh trade bold rap verses, their delivery swaggering and infectious. Pablo’s wordplay turns the everyday Filipino phrase “_doon ka_” (“go over there”) into a playful, defiant refrain—a winking incantation to repel bad vibes, dead weight, and unwanted forces.

Advertisement

The effect is both jubilant and cutting. If the song is an invitation to join the revelry, it is also a gatekeeping spell: only those who belong, who understand, may stay.

      ![Image 10: sb19](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/VMAN-SB19-2.jpg?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

on josh, pablo, ken, and stell:  
all clothing _**tod’s**_ / jewelry _**bvlgari**_

—

on justin:

all clothing _**brunello cucinelli**_ / jewelry _**bvlgari**_

Yet beyond its aesthetic bravado and sonic innovation, _DUNGKA!_ is significant because it refuses to dilute itself. It is deeply and stubbornly local, packed with references that demand fluency, but offered generously enough to welcome newcomers. It is a pop star flex, but also an archival act: a documentation of how Filipinos live, love, eat, protest, and endure.

In an era when many artists aspire to cross borders by sanding down their cultural particularities, SB19 does the opposite. They dig deeper. And somehow, in doing so, they make their music—and their movement—feel not just national, but planetary.

After all, specificity is what makes universality possible. In the chaotic beauty of _DUNGKA!_, SB19 reminds us that the more vividly you show your own world, the more the world will want to see.

The sound reverberated continuously during the speech, and later it gradually extended to the meaning of the very moving music at the ceremony. People believe that the sound of the conch is as sacred as Buddha throughout the universe. Temple bells, wax incense, bonfires... these are highlanders play the important role in their daily rituals, it helps focus and concentrate the energies of our own thoughts.

As for the DUNGKA's brand philosophy, we explore the new contemporary interpretation, a new Tibetan style designed that would gives life energy. The founding team members of the brand has relevant backgrounds in overseas market operation, product development and design, and art trend influence. After many trips to the Himalayas, the team members burst into creative inspiration and turned the unique sensory aesthetic into a series of fragrances and home products.

Through the replacement of traditional Tibetan sign elements, the team members creatively breaks through regional limitations while retaining its past style, and the series of classic logos with Himalayan characteristics can be used and displayed more harmoniously and flexibly in urban homes, making the space more oriental of new modern tone.

Practicality, simplicity and stability are the core philosophies of all DUNGKA products. Whether at home or on the way, the products could infuse energy in your mind and soul. It can always accompany you forward, assist you to feel every moment of earnestness and comfort, and give you a comfortable, relaxing and healing experience.

4.content:
SB19 didn’t just show up to sing and dance. They came to shake the room, throw a giant party, sprinkle in life lessons, and leave us thinking about it for days. “Dungka” is not just a song or a video. It is a whole moment in pop culture. If you have seen it, you know. If you have not, well, you are seriously missing out.

Here are five reasons why fans can’t stop calling this MV iconic.

**1\. It is a Hidden Treasure Chest of Meaning**

At first glance, “Dungka” looks like a chaotic street party. Balloons everywhere. Crazy dance battles. Zumba in the parking lot. But fans quickly caught on that every scene means something. “Dungka” is slangy for “doon ka,” which means “go there” or “go away” in Tagalog, and in Hiligaynon, it can also mean “to arrive at port.” It is all about movement, journeys, and facing where life takes you.

Scenes like Ghost Wrecker gobbling down a crab are not just funny. That is a jab at “crab mentality,” where people pull each other down instead of lifting each other up. Zumba classes and the winks at breaking gender roles. Rap battles? That is the spirit of Filipino street smarts, creativity, and fighting through words instead of fists.

Every colorful moment hits you with something deeper if you look just a little closer.

**2\. They Took Shots at Society in the Most Fun Way Possible**

Most songs that talk about problems tend to get really heavy. But SB19 managed to clap back at all the negativity like judgment, stereotyping, and cancel culture without making it feel like homework. It is fun, but the message is loud and clear. Society loves to judge, but you do not have to live your life by their rules.

Instead of preaching, they are like that one friend who jokes about everything but secretly gives the best advice when you are about to make a dumb life choice.

**3\. The Guest List Was a Whole Party by Itself**

Let us get this straight. SB19 did not just invite random people. They brought out legends, icons, and people who each represent something beautiful about Filipino culture. And they showed up in this order:

*   [Ghost Wrecker](https://www.facebook.com/ghostwrecker28/) — gaming legend
*   [Kween Yasmin](https://www.facebook.com/www.facebookyasminasistido.090/) — hilarious and vibrant online personality
*   [Malupiton](https://www.facebook.com/borgerkasakenboy/) — master of witty content
*   [Smugglaz](https://www.facebook.com/Smugglaz187MOB/) — a rap king
*   [Shehyee](https://www.facebook.com/shehyee/) — another rap champ
*   [Alodia Gosiengfiao](https://www.facebook.com/AlodiaGosiengfiao/) — queen of cosplay
*   [Mimiyuuuh](https://www.facebook.com/mimiyuuuh/) — fashionista and comedian rolled into one
*   [Pat Lasaten](https://www.instagram.com/patlasaten/?hl=en) — from Ben&Ben, musical genius
*   [Agnes Reoma](https://www.instagram.com/agnesreoma/?hl=en) — also from Ben&Ben, making magic on the bass
*   [Maymay Entrata](https://www.instagram.com/maymay/?hl=en) — actress, model, and overall star
*   [Sassa Gurl](https://www.facebook.com/Sassagurl/) — queen of online humor and sass
*   [Jayat](https://www.facebook.com/JayatGamingTV/) — fresh face from the rap battle scene
*   [Vice Ganda](https://www.instagram.com/praybeytbenjamin/?hl=en) — comedian royalty and LGBTQ+ icon

Each guest was not just there to pose for the camera. They were woven into the story. It felt like a real community, a huge melting pot of different talents and personalities. Just like the Philippines itself.

**4\. It Was the Most Filipino Thing Ever**

No glammed-up skyscrapers. No rented supercars. No trying to look international. “Dungka” was all about us. The streets, the games, the music, the crazy, happy, everyday life of being Pinoy.

There were street courts, carinderia scenes, fliptop battles, Zumba sessions, messy barkadahan moments, and yes, even the karaoke we all know and love. SB19 showed that being Filipino is already world-class. No filters needed.

**5\. It Gave the Biggest, Sassiest Middle Finger to Negativity**

At the heart of everything, “Dungka” tells you this. Life is tough. People will judge you, laugh at you, and try to pull you down. But who cares? Go live your life anyway. Wear what you want. Dance how you feel. Be loud. Be soft. Be whoever the heck you want to be.

That is the real magic of this MV. It was not about pretending everything is perfect. It was about dancing through the mess and living despite the critics. Fans said it felt like being handed a mic and told, “Your voice matters too. Now go sing your heart out.”

Dungka is not just a music video. It is a love letter to everyone who has ever been judged, doubted, or told to shrink themselves. SB19 basically said, “Nah. You are bigger than that. Let us celebrate.”

And honestly? We are so here for it.

1.content:
![Image 1](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/z5sfb61RHP2RjMjrH3l_qA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTEyNDI7aD04Mjg7Y2Y9d2VicA--/https://media.zenfs.com/en/billboard_547/a42e3a4eef278f81d9d212828aa86091)

![Image 2: The Dream Setlist for SB19’s Simula at Wakas World Tour](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/NlOayqtlR.HAj605acS.hA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTYzNTtjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/billboard_547/20350a81543839948863c64532360394)

The Dream Setlist for SB19’s Simula at Wakas World Tour

The last time [SB19](https://billboard.com/music/sb19) headed out on an international trek was for the Pagtatag! World Tour in 2023, where the Filipino-pop group played 18 shows throughout four countries across the Philippines, United States, Canada, Japan, and the United Arab Emirates. Following the release of the group’s _Simula at Wakas_ EP, which saw lead single “DAM” score them their first No. 1 on a U.S. _Billboard_ chart earlier this year, the quintet is gearing up for an even bigger worldwide tour.

**More from Billboard**

[As](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/sb19-set-simula-wakas-world-020000188.html) _[Billboard](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/sb19-set-simula-wakas-world-020000188.html)_ [exclusively revealed](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/sb19-set-simula-wakas-world-020000188.html) in February, SB19 set 19 dates on the Simula at Wakas World Tour, spanning cities in the Philippines, Taiwan, the U.S., Singapore, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE this year. In addition to playing some of the biggest venues of the group’s career, SB19 teased more cities and shows to be announced soon, with visits to Australia, Japan, and Hong Kong on the horizon.

**Pablo**, **Josh**, **Ken**, **Stell** and **Justin** previously told _Billboard_ that their fans, known as A’TIN, should “stay tuned for new genres and performances, plus fresh arrangements of our older tracks,” adding how that “from our last tour they have seen more of our individuality but this time, we will be coming stronger.”

A stronger, bigger tour naturally requires a stronger, bigger setlist. So, before the group plays the first dates across Asia this spring, and returns to the U.S. in July, here is _Billboard’s_ dream setlist for the upcoming Simula at Wakas World Tour, which will hopefully include most, if not all, of these global hits.

“DAM (Extended Ver.)”
---------------------

The opening number is _the_ song that sets the tone for your whole tour and “DAM” is the clear choice for several reasons. Not only is it the lead single off SB19’s recently released _Simula at Wakas_ EP, but the song scored the group their first No. 1 on a U.S. Billboard song sales chart following its debut atop the [World Digital Song Sales chart](https://www.billboard.com/charts/world-digital-song-sales/) in March.

But “DAM” didn’t only resonate in the U.S., but hit No. 4 on the recently launched [Billboard Philippines Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-philippines-hot-100/), and bowed on charts in the U.K., New Zealand, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and more. What better song to kick off your new worldwide tour than your biggest global hit yet?

Naturally, we want to hear the extended version of the song because its military-style march opening feels like a truly epic way to kick off the show.

“8TonBall”
----------

Continuing the high energy set by “DAM,” the next move would be to jump right into another new SB19 banger with “8onBall.” Not only will it keep the audience hyped, but also express the group’s greater global ambitions amid their largest world tour yet. As declared by Justin and Josh in the song’s intro: “Wait a second, ’cause we’re going to the top.”

“Shooting for the Stars”
------------------------

To connect to the theme of SB19’s worldwide ambitions while keeping the audience excited, “Shooting for the Stars” is our next pick. The August Rigo–penned lyrics will ring true to the tone of the concert (“I’ve been shooting for the stars, aimin’ high/ The universe is ours, yours and mine/ Hop up on this rocket, nothing’s gonna stop it, no”) while the addictive post-chorus hook is begging for an entire venue to singalong (“High! Oh yeah!/ Ready, aim, fire, shoot! Oh, yeah!”).

“I Want You”
------------

After three songs of what will surely be intense choreography, we’ll give the guys a break by slowing things down with the other song August Rigo wrote for them, 2023’s “I Want You” from their _Pagtatag!_ album, with the mid-tempo R&B jam allowing the guys a moment to catch their breath, greet the audience and focus on the passionate delivery and honeyed harmonies. The guys can bring out the mic stands or stools to sit to enhance the song’s intimate, sultry vibe.

“DUNGKA!”
---------

Time to turn the volume back up. The latest single off SB19’s _Simula at Wakas_ EP — which made its debut on [World Digital Song Sales](https://www.billboard.com/charts/world-digital-song-sales/2025-05-10/) earlier this month following its music video release — would be a natural pick here. After “I Want You,” we could imagine the guys ducking out for an outfit change at this point to give them some additional breathing room and signify the show’s next chapter of intensity. We’d love to see looks reminiscent of the fun and colorful looks the guys wore in the video.

“KALAKAL”
---------

Since the group’s 2023 Pagtatag! World Tour, the group has been delivering some of the best collaborations of their careers. “KALAKAL” with Filipino hip-hop icon Gloc 9 feels like a must-include for this tour, especially since the critically acclaimed veteran made a special appearance at the group’s previous world tour finale in early 2024.

Stell will set a powerful tone with his opening lines, “You can’t stop this, we gonna get it /Who can? None, ’cause we born to take it,” and we’d love to see if either of SB19’s top rappers Pablo or Josh might want to attempt to rap Gloc 9’s lines, or even write new verses whenever Gloc isn’t on hand to perform with them.

“Alab (Burning)” (New Version)
------------------------------

As promised by Josh in SB19’s exclusive interview with _Billboard_, the group will be delivering new versions of their past material, and we’d love to hear a fresh interpretation of the early SB19 single “Alab (Burning).” While the bright electro-pop track might not feel mature enough for where the group stands today (and didn’t make the cut for the Pagtatag! World Tour), taking the song’s theme of “Burning” and giving it a rock, hip-hop or EDM makeover would surely add some edge, while also serving as a nostalgic treat for those A’TIN who have been with the guys since the beginning.

“Mapa”
------

Some felt the Pagtatag! World Tour’s setlist was too front-loaded with too many ballads. But no matter what you thought about the song order, the gorgeous dedication to parents, “Mapa,” was a standout moment, with the entire venue singing along to the soulful singalong hook. We’ll gladly take an extended live version of “Mapa” here to ensure everyone gets their ballad fix.

“The Boy Who Cried Wolf”/ “Edsa”/”Butata” (Pablo Solo Stage)
------------------------------------------------------------

To truly show how much the group has grown, this feels like a perfect moment to introduce some solo stages. For an easy sonic transition from the fuzzy feelings set by “Mapa,” we’d love SB19 leader Pablo’s performance to begin with a snippet of his stunning, slow-burning ballad “The Boy Who Cried Wolf.” While the song (and its accompanying video) are especially emotional, letting Pablo give a taste of the track and the lingering wolf-like “woo, ooh” hook before the regal trumps of his empowering single “Edsa” take over. Pablo can showcase his pop sensibilities on the bright track for a moment before transitioning into the much darker rap cut “Batata,” which lays out his ambitions over zipping, pounding production.

Pablo had a busy 2024, dropping “Edsa” in May before unleashing both his _ALON_ and _LAON_ albums within a week of each other in September, so it’s the perfect time to show his breadth of work. While we’re not entirely sure how to make the jump from the stark “Boy Who Cried Wolf” to cheery “Edsa” and then the intensity of “Butata,” if anyone could figure it out, it’s SB19’s genius producer Pablo.

“Fake Faces” (Ken Solo Stage)
-----------------------------

Continuing with a heavier theme set from Pablo’s “La Luna,” we’d love to see Ken — a.k.a. Felip — hit the stage next to deliver a song like 2024’s “Fake Faces.” The alt-rock rager can be a moment of release for the audience to really let go and feel ready to truly enjoy the rest of the night without worrying about what anyone might think.

“1999” (Josh Cullen Solo Stage)
-------------------------------

Playing off the rock vibes in “Fake Faces,” Josh Cullen gets his rock-star moment with a performance of his popular single “1999” from his _Lost & Found_ album. It’s another moment for fans to rock out with the guys. We might be crazy, but we could even imagine Josh crowd-surfing while belting out the track. Too much? We’d imagine not for Josh.

“Time”
------

After the members get some sufficient rest after the three solo stages, it feels right to bring out _Simula at Wakas_‘ intense ballad “Time.” The track features an impressive vocal performance with a few starts and stops in the arrangement, which will require the guys to be fully prepared to tackle the all-English cut.

“Golden Hour (SB19 Remix)”
--------------------------

As part of SB19’s continuing international crossover, the band linked up with JVKE for a special remix of his [Billboard Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/) Top 10 hit “Golden Hour.” While JVKE raced up the charts around the world with “Golden Hour” in 2023 (reaching its No. 13 peak on the [B](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[i](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[l](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[l](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[b](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[o](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[a](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[r](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[d](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/) [G](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/)[lobal 200](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-global-200/) in February), SB19’s remix helped extend the song’s impact and longevity, with an SB19-only performance being a particular treat for international audiences. Maybe JVKE could even pop by for a special appearance at one of the stops.

“What?” (New Version)
---------------------

It’s time to kick back up the energy with a familiar, fan-favorite single like “What?” Upon its release in 2021, the team that produced the track with Pablo shared how the song was particularly challenging to craft due to the multiple tempo changes. A new version that imagines the song slightly more straightforward allows fans to enjoy while taking it easier on SB19, who are, at this point, only about halfway through the concert.

“Mana”
------

Despite never being released as a single, “Mana” remains one of SB19’s most-streamed tracks on Spotify with the trap-y throbber becoming one of the group’s go-to live tracks.

“Bazinga”
---------

“Bazinga” is our pick to follow, keeping the energy from “Mana” alive and connecting as yet another fire track from the _Pagsibol_ EP, the final song from the 2021 record in this concert.

“CRIMZONE”
----------

SB19 have shared that they considered releasing “CRIMZONE” as the lead single off _PAGTATAG!_ (though ultimately going with “Gento”), but another fan-favorite cut that has surpassed the Spotify streams of several of the group’s singles, it would truly be a crime not to include “CRIMZONE” and is one last big up-tempo before — dream setlist spoiler! — another set of solo stages.

“Surreal”/”Kaibigan” (Justin Solo Stages)
-----------------------------------------

Justin delivered a lovely cover of One Direction’s “Little Things” during the Pagtatag! World Tour, but now SB19’s youngest member gets a chance to show how much he’s grown since the last tour by releasing his own solo music and kicking off his acting career. We’d love to hear a medley of his easy-listening rock-pop tracks “Surreal” and “Kaibigan” during his solo moment — perhaps cutting the first 30 seconds of the latter since it may be challenging to get a similar reverb and jumping straight into the joyous pre-chorus before encouraging the audience to clap along on the singalong hook.

“Room” (Stell Solo Stage)
-------------------------

Stell took the audience’s breath away with his powerhouse performance of “Defying Gravity” (performing all parts from the _Wicked_ epic) every night on the Pagtatag! World Tour. We’re looking for him to stun us once again by recreating the performance showcased in his funky 2024 single “Room” — including, most importantly, the mesmerizingly cool chair dance he pulls off during the bridge. Take a look below in case you haven’t already.

“Ready”
-------

Another crossover moment from SB19’s past year includes their featuring on a single from apl.de.ap, the Black Eyed Peas Philippines-born member who has represented his heritage by rapping in Tagalog in BEP tracks like “Bebop” and “The Apl Song.”

This bumping dance track is a perfect song to transition back to the group music after Justin and Stell take the stage. Lyrics like “Get ready for the night, you ready?/ I’ve been waiting for this night for so long” will hit with slightly harder impact when fans realize the concert is inevitably coming to a close soon after months of anticipation, but will inevitably snap into dance mode once the beat hits on the second chorus.

“Go Up”/”Moonlight”
-------------------

In a full display of how far SB19 has come in their five years together, we’d love to hear their early EDM single “Go Up” mashed up with “Moonlight,” their latest DJ collaboration with U.S.-based producers Ian Asher and Terry Zhong. Both songs feature euphoric, feel-good builds, and it feels like a special and clever way to represent artistic growth while giving newer A’TIN more reasons to revisit older material.

“Quit”
------

There’s one more new song left to perform from _Simula at Wakas_ with “Quit” acting as the EP’s centerpiece rock anthem. At four minutes and forty-three seconds, it’s by far the longest song on the record, and the layers of harmonies on the bridge are perfect for the members to lead an epic singalong with the audience as they wave goodbye to the audience…

Encore: “Gento”
---------------

…but that goodbye will be short-lived because it’s encore time!

SB19 used “What?” as their final encore song on the Pagtatag! World Tour, bringing back the beloved breakout single as an official, satisfying closer for the show. We want to recreate the wonderful energy of that moment again, but this time with _Pagtatag_‘s lead single, “Gento,” which helped the group break out even bigger and will reignite the crowd once they hear its opening beats.

Encore: “WYAT (Where You At)”
-----------------------------

Because everything needs to be bigger on this tour, SB19 won’t just have one encore song but two! Ending with the band’s feel-good funk-pop single, “WYAT (Where You At),” feels appropriate, as the lyrics discuss searching for one’s other half to complete them. Pablo, Ken, Josh, Stell, and Justin can dedicate the song to fans as a final message to officially wrap up their biggest show to date.

Find out more information about — and see what songs SB19 really performs — with more details on the [Wakas World Tour here](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/sb19-set-simula-wakas-world-020000188.html).

![Image 1: SB19: ‘Dungka!’ sa Mayon](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/files/2025/06/Lifestyle1042661-1200x800.jpg)

SB19 —TOURISM PROMOTIONS BOARD

While not extraordinarily rare, a clear sighting of Mayon Volcano isn’t always guaranteed. But when she does reveal herself—her peak unshrouded by clouds, her perfect cone cutting against the blue skies—the picture she paints is nothing short of a blessing. Or, as Bicolano folklore suggests, a sign of warm welcome.

On June 14, Mayon stood in all her majesty, as if awaiting the P-pop sensation **[SB19](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/615958/sb19-stuns-taiwans-hito-music-awards-2025-stage-with-fiery-performance)**’s arrival in the province of Albay, where they headlined the opening night of the Bicol Music Festival. It’s hard not to think of this moment as a stroke of serendipity: an enduring natural icon playing host to a rising cultural force.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

The parallels didn’t stop there.

All around Legazpi City and its neighboring towns, the volcano was an inescapable sight—her peak jutting above rooftops, her symmetry on full display from open fields. And on the way to the venue—a sprawling festival ground on what was once the old Legazpi Airport—Mayon beckoned from the horizon. SB19 is just as ubiquitous: their songs echo across the nation and far beyond; their faces a familiar presence, from social media feeds to billboards lining major streets.

Mayon, with her violent eruptions throughout history, has shaped and reshaped her surrounding landscape many times over. SB19’s power is more figurative than destructive—but no less transformative. Brimming with talent and burning with purpose, the group has been redefining the conventions of local pop music with sounds and concepts fueled by foresight and imagination: a beacon in the P-pop movement’s steady march.

Deafening screams
-----------------

The sun had already set by the time SB19 took the stage. Still, Mayon’s unmistakable silhouette loomed, watching as her guests—Pablo, Stell, Ken, Justin, and Josh—lit up the stage with a fire all their own. And the moment they emerged, the crowd—despite having endured the heat and long hours on their feet earlier in the day—sprang to life, erupting into deafening screams.

Presented by the Tourism Promotions Board, the Department of Tourism, and Live Nation Philippines, the show—mounted as part of the “Love the Philippines” campaign—aimed to boost concert tourism nationwide. They couldn’t have chosen a better draw. More than 12,000 fans attended, some of whom came from Aurora, Zambales, Metro Manila, and even Thailand—a testament to how, like Mayon’s community-building role and touristic appeal, SB19 attracts visitors wherever they go, bringing people together in celebration of music.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

Similarly, the band values visiting places outside Manila, making it easier for their beloved A’tin (fandom name) across the country to see them live. “Good thing we were given a chance to go here, to go to you. Because usually, it’s the other way around,” Stell told the crowd, who earlier enjoyed performances by Fred Engay, Dwta, Kim Ji-soo, Kim Won-shik, and Earl Agustin.

After their recent “Simula at Wakas” world tour kickoff at the Philippine Arena—a landmark two-day event marked by expansive productions, intricate stage designs, and cinematic visuals—this show was markedly pared down, as expected in a festival setting. In a way, it felt like a microcosm of what fans might see on the group’s upcoming international tour dates, which—as they themselves noted—will be more modest in scale due to logistical and venue constraints.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

And yet, the hallmarks that make SB19 such compelling performers remained intact: vocal prowess, explosive choreography, commanding stage presence—all proof that spectacle isn’t a prerequisite for impact. Because if there’s one thing you can expect from SB19, it’s this: no matter the size of the venue, they will unfailingly deliver with equal fervor.

![Image 2: SB19: ‘Dungka!’ sa Mayon](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/files/2025/06/Lifestyle1042687-1.jpg)

Stell poses with the Mayon Volcano while on a morning jog.— @STELL16 INSTAGRAM

Lean and mean set list
----------------------

The set list was lean and mean, blending high-octane tracks that had the crowd dancing, with emotional ballads that inspired poignant sing-alongs. Bops like “Dam,” “8TonBall,” and “Dungka!” brought out the group’s natural grit and swagger. Meanwhile, mid-tempos like “Quit,” “Time,” and “Mapa” let their vocals and soulful harmonies take center stage—a soothing salve between the bursts of energy.

But more than the performances, it was the moments between songs that showed why they’ve attracted such a massive and fiercely loyal following. Every exchange and bit of goofing around onstage felt heartwarming and spontaneous. You didn’t just listen to the conversations—they let you in—and in the process, made the wide-open field feel like an intimate shared space.

It’s in the way they learned Bicolano phrases to connect deeper with local fans; the way they jokingly roasted their fans (“Wala kayo sa tono,” Pablo quipped); and how they quickly responded to a call for a medic, with Stell reminding everyone to keep their distance with a witty riposte: “Stare at the person beside you and say, ‘Dungka!’”

Just as the crowd thought the show was over, not a few eager fans made a mad dash backstage—only to scramble back to the pit when SB19 returned for an encore of “Gento.” This time, even those who hadn’t planned on watching were dancing—the medics, utility crew, and security staff included. Casuals went home as newly converted fans; the A’tin left with their love and admiration reaffirmed.

It’s this very feeling that SB19 hopes to awaken in their fans time and time again. Still riding high from a string of iconic projects and performances, the band already has their sights set on something bigger and better. Coachella? Lollapalooza? Only time will tell. But one thing is certain: they’re determined to become even better versions of themselves.

“It will be hard to surpass what we’ve done. Sinagad na namin. But we want bigger innovations… bigger and grander stages,” Pablo told select reporters backstage, where fellow performers waited outside their tent, eager to meet them and ask for photos.

Just as Mayon stands steeped in myth and legend, SB19 is still building their own. And with every new chapter and turn of the page, it’s their self-belief and unwavering fans who serve as the ink with which they write their own story.

“We’re here today because of hard work, sweat, and tears. We’ve been through a lot. We want to show that we can do it, so that others believe that they can do it, too… even if you come from a humble background,” Ken told Lifestyle. “That’s what we hope to convey. To show your best. That you may have no regrets because you tried.” /_**edv**_

"**Dungka!**" (stylized in [all uppercase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_caps "All caps")) is a song recorded by the Filipino boy band [SB19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SB19 "SB19") for their third [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP), _[Simula at Wakas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simula_at_Wakas "Simula at Wakas")_ (2025). The band's leader, [Pablo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_/(Filipino_musician/) "Pablo (Filipino musician)"), wrote the song and co-produced it with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase. It is an [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") [diss track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_/(music/) "Diss (music)") aimed at haters, with lyrics demanding them to leave, uttering the phrase "_doon ka_" (lit. 'go over there'). "Dungka!" is listed as the sixth track on the EP, which [Sony Music Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Philippines "Sony Music Philippines") released on April 25, 2025.

"Dungka!" received favorable reviews from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism"), who complimented Pablo's songwriting and his use of [wordplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_play "Word play"). The song was an entry to [record charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_chart "Record chart"); it peaked at number 21 on the [Philippines Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_Hot_100 "Philippines Hot 100") and number 7 on [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [World Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Digital_Song_Sales "World Digital Song Sales"). The accompanying [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), directed by Kerbs Balagtas, featured [Filipino culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_the_Philippines "Culture of the Philippines") and depicted the band in the streets showing allegiance to their community while opposing an antagonist who threatened the locals. SB19 promoted the song with live performances and included it on the [set list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list") of their [Simula at Wakas World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simula_at_Wakas_World_Tour "Simula at Wakas World Tour") (2025). "Dungka!" received multiple accolades, including a [Filipino Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_Music_Awards "Filipino Music Awards") for Pop Song of the Year.

Background and release
----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dungka!&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

[![Image 3: A group photo of SB19 onstage, each with a handheld microphone](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/SB19_on_stage_at_the_Pagtatag%21_World_Tour%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-SB19_on_stage_at_the_Pagtatag%21_World_Tour%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SB19_on_stage_at_the_Pagtatag!_World_Tour,_2023_/(cropped/).jpg)

SB19 during the [Pagtatag! World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pagtatag!_World_Tour "Pagtatag! World Tour") in 2023

The Filipino boy band [SB19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SB19 "SB19") released their first [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP), _[Pagsibol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pagsibol "Pagsibol")_ (lit. 'growth'), in 2021,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Lago-2021-1) exploring genres such as [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), and [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music"), departing from the [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop") production from their debut [studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album"), _[Get in the Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_in_the_Zone "Get in the Zone")_ (2020).[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Lago-2021-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-2) [Pablo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_/(Filipino_musician/) "Pablo (Filipino musician)"), the band's leader, revealed in an interview with [Zach Sang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Sang "Zach Sang") that _Pagsibol_ and their future releases are part of a [trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilogy "Trilogy"), the others being _[Pagtatag!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pagtatag! "Pagtatag!")_ (lit. 'strengthening') and _[Simula at Wakas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simula_at_Wakas "Simula at Wakas")_ (lit. 'beginning and end').[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-3) In 2023, the group released their second EP, _Pagtatag!_, the trilogy's second installment.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-4) The EP includes the single, "[Gento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gento_/(song/) "Gento (song)")" (2023),[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-5) which scored their first entry to two [record charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_chart "Record chart"),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-PhilippinesSongs-7) including in the Philippines, where the single peaked at number eight.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-PhilippinesSongs-7) The following year, they confirmed during the premiere night for [_Pagtatag!: The Documentary_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pagtatag!_World_Tour "Pagtatag! World Tour") (2024) that they are currently working with _Simula at Wakas_.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-8)

On January 31, 2025, SB19 published a trailer via their social media accounts. In it, they revealed the title of their third EP, _Simula and Wakas_, and announced its release date.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-9) The EP's [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single"), "[Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam_/(song/) "Dam (song)")", was released ahead of the EP on February 28,[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-10) achieving commercial success.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-12) On April 7, the band announced the EP's track list, along with the names of the songwriters and producers involved in the record. Out of seven tracks in the EP, "Dungka!" is listed as track six.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-13) [Sony Music Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Philippines "Sony Music Philippines") released _Simula at Wakas_ on April 25 through [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") and [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") formats.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Saulog-2025-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Junaini-2025-15)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-SimulaAtWakasAppleMusic-16)

Composition and lyrics
----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dungka!&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrics")\]

![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Gnome-mime-sound-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-sound-openclipart.svg.png)

"Dungka!" is a [diss track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_/(music/) "Diss (music)") with lyrics urging haters to go away. Music critics noted the song's loud production.

"Dungka!" is 3 minutes and 35 seconds in length.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-SimulaAtWakasAppleMusic-16) Pablo, the band's leader, wrote the song by himself and co-produced it with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase; they also [mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_/(recorded_music/) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") and [mastered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastering_/(audio/) "Mastering (audio)") the song together.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Dungka!MV-17) The song's title, "Dungka!", is a [wordplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_play "Word play") derived from the [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language") phrase "_doon ka_", which translates to "go over there" in English, a motif that served as a [refrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain") in the song's lyrics.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Aduna-2025-18) Musically, it is a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") song with elements of [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno"), [hyperpop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperpop "Hyperpop") and [rave music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rave_music "Rave music"),[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Saulog-2025-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Junaini-2025-15)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19) accompanied by [catchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catchiness "Catchiness") pounding beats.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Aduna-2025-18)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Llemit-2025-20) Rome Saenz of _[Billboard Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Philippines "Billboard Philippines")_ described the song's production as "blaring \[and\] sharp",[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Saenz-2025-21) while Rafael Bautista of _[Nylon Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon_/(magazine/) "Nylon (magazine)")_ and _Preview_'s Kyla Villena describing it as "loud".[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22)

Lyrically, "Dungka!" is interpreted as a [diss track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_/(music/) "Diss (music)") against SB19's haters,[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Roxas-2025-23)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Miranda-2025-24) responding to the criticisms and [name-calling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_calling "Name calling") imposed on them,[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22) and those who are doubting their capabilities.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Xianna-2025-25) In the lyrics, the phrase "_doon ka_" is prominent, a common Filipino expression that signifies displeasure,[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Llemit-2025-20) which was used in the song to convey that negativity and undesirable people are unwelcome and should leave.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Aduna-2025-18)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Gomez-2025-26) Other lyrics also follow a similar theme, like "_Kung 'di mo 'to gusto, tumabi ka d'yan_" (lit. 'If you do not like this, move out of the way'), further insisting that their critics should go away.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Roxas-2025-23)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Xianna-2025-25)

"Dungka!" received favorable reviews from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism"), many of whom complimented Pablo's songwriting. Writing for _[The Philippine Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Philippine_Star "The Philippine Star")_, Kathleen Llemit noted Pablo's preference for using wordplay, adding that she considers it a "testament to \[his\] songwriting skills".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Llemit-2025-20) Ann Jenireene Gomez of the [_Daily Tribune_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_Tribune_/(Philippines/) "Daily Tribune (Philippines)") described the use of wordplay "witty" and a "cheeky way to shoo away negative energy",[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Gomez-2025-26) while Dayne Aduna of [_VMan Southeast Asia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMan "VMan") regard it as a playful way to alter an everyday Filipino phrase.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Aduna-2025-18) The song's noisy production was also a key topic, with critics noting that, despite it sounding loud, _Nylon Manila_'s Rafael Bautista opined that the noise still resonates in a good way._[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)_ Rome Saenz of _Billboard Philippines_ considered the song "irresistibly catchy", despite its noisy production.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Saenz-2025-21) [_Inquirer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Daily_Inquirer "Philippine Daily Inquirer")'s Pauline Miranda also compared it with the group's 2021 single "[Bazinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bazinga_/(song/) "Bazinga (song)")", which she referred to as its "more fun \[and\] unbothered brother".[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Miranda-2025-24) _Bandwagon_'s Hidzir Junaini opined that "Dungka!" is a surprising track in the EP,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Junaini-2025-15) while Bautista finds it as one of the tracks that stood out from _Simula at Wakas.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)_

Commercially, "Dungka!" was an entry for SB19 on [record charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_chart "Record chart") upon the release of _Simula at Wakas_. In the Philippines, the song entered two _Billboard Philippines_ charts, debuting and peaking at number 21 on the [Philippines Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_Hot_100 "Philippines Hot 100") and number 14 on the Top Philippine Songs during the week of May 10, 2025.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Saenz-2025b-27)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-BBPHTPS-28) The song spent a total of 12 weeks on the Philippines Hot 100 and 3 weeks on the Top Philippine Songs charts.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-BBPHTPS-28)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-BBPHHot100-29) In the same week, the song debuted and peaked at number seven on [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [World Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Digital_Song_Sales "World Digital Song Sales") chart, marking their third entry on the chart, following "Gento" and "Dam".[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Saenz-2025b-27)

Kerbs Balagtas directed the accompanying [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Dungka!",[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Gomez-2025-26)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-ABSCBNNews-2025-36) which was [surprise-released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surprise_album "Surprise album") on April 25, 2025, on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), the same day as the release of _Simula at Wakas_.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Llemit-2025-20) The music video is themed around [street credibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_credibility "Street credibility") and is set in the chaotic streets of [Metro Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Manila "Metro Manila"),[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Pare%C3%B1o-2025-37) depicting SB19 showing their allegiance to the local community.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Pare%C3%B1o-2025-37) They were circumventing around the antagonist, played by social media personality Ghost Wrecker, who taunts and threatens the locals,[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Pare%C3%B1o-2025-37) with people later coming together to oppose him.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Liong-2025-38) The video also showed activities relevant to the [Filipino culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_the_Philippines "Culture of the Philippines"), including [Zumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zumba "Zumba"), [street food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_food "Street food"), activism, [street basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streetball "Streetball"), [karaoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaoke "Karaoke"), [ten-twenty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_games_in_the_Philippines "Traditional games in the Philippines"),[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Aduna-2025-18)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Gomez-2025-26)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-39) and band members participating in a [battle rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_rap "Battle rap").[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22) The group also gathered together to raise social awareness, raising posters and signs with text including "_Iangat ang sining na Pilipino_" (lit. 'Elevate Filipino art') and "_Sining ang sandata sa kulturang mapagpalaya_" (lit. 'Art is the weapon in a liberating culture').[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Roxas-2025-23)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Xianna-2025-25)

The music video received favorable reviews for depicting Filipino culture.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Gomez-2025-26)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Pare%C3%B1o-2025-37) It was regarded as a tribute to individuality, community, diversity, and everyday life, while calling out negativity and raising one's voice for change.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Liong-2025-38) Writers highlighted a scene from the video where the antagonist was eating a crab, which they interpreted as a symbol for [crab mentality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crab_mentality "Crab mentality") among Filipinos.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Bautista-2025-19)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Xianna-2025-25) [Shehyee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shehyee "Shehyee") and Smugglaz, cosplayer [Alodia Gosiengfiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alodia_Gosiengfiao "Alodia Gosiengfiao"), gamer Jayat, and social media personalities [Kween Yasmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kween_Yasmin "Kween Yasmin"), [Malupiton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malupiton "Malupiton"), Gurl"),[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-Villena-2025-22) all of whom the band had collaborated with to help spread a message about diversity and uniqueness among Live performances and other use
-------------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dungka!&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Live performances and other use")\]

Following the release of _Simula at Wakas_, SB19 arranged a surprise [flash mob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_mob "Flash mob") in [Bonifacio Global City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonifacio_Global_City "Bonifacio Global City") in [Taguig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taguig "Taguig") on April 25 and performed the song with "Dam".[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-41) The band followed it with a television performance of "Dungka!" during their appearance on the variety show [_It's Showtime_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_Showtime_/(Philippine_TV_program/) "It's Showtime (Philippine TV program)") on April 26.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-42) On May 7, the group appeared on the [Wish 107.5 Bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DWNU "DWNU"), performing a three-song [set list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list"). It includes "Dungka!", which they performed it on a makeshift stage outside the bus.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-43) In support of the EP, SB19 embarked on their third world tour, the [Simula at Wakas World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simula_at_Wakas_World_Tour "Simula at Wakas World Tour") (2025), with the song included on its set list.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-44)

SB19 appeared at the [Hito Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hito_Music_Awards "Hito Music Awards") 2025 in Taiwan on June 21, performing the song during the ceremony.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-45) The band went to [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy and served as a guest performer at the Sama sa Roma 2025 event on October 12, where "Dungka!" among the songs they performed.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-46)[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-47) On November 30, the group performed the song during their [halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halftime_show "Halftime show") at the [_Honor of Kings_ International Championship 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor_of_Kings "Honor of Kings") held at the [Ayala Malls Manila Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayala_Malls_Manila_Bay "Ayala Malls Manila Bay") in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque").[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-48) Shortly after, they went to [Kaohsiung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaohsiung "Kaohsiung"), Taiwan to perform at the [ACON 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10th_Asia_Artist_Awards "10th Asia Artist Awards") festival held at the [Kaohsiung National Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Stadium_/(Kaohsiung/) "National Stadium (Kaohsiung)") on December 7, where they performed four songs, including "Dungka!".[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-49)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-50)

In other uses, a snippet of the song was featured in a video uploaded in June by [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") on [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok").[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-51) The song was also featured in a music video for the 2025 video game _[Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatal_Fury:_City_of_the_Wolves "Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves")_.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungka!#cite_note-52)

SB19’s Dungka! Of haters and trapos

![Image 2: SB19](https://www.bulatlat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/IMG_0472-e1745717547903.jpeg)

Screenshot from SB19's Dungka! music video

by [Bulatlat Contributors](https://www.bulatlat.com/author/contributors/)

Published on Apr 27, 2025

Last Updated on Apr 28, 2025 at 8:04 am

ADVERTISEMENT

By YANNI ROXAS

In the heat of the electoral campaign surprisingly comes _Dungka!_ (urban slang for “Doon Ka”), a music video (mv) by the phenomenal SB19 that takes a dig at bashers and trapos alike while celebrating and showcasing Pinoy pop culture.

Pop here is “pangmasa, pangkalye,‘tol”  and affirms SB19’s confidence and comfort in their humble beginnings. It is as if it was their own typical Pinoy community, a mix of loud people, engaging, and huddling not just in their homes but especially on the streets.  Sellers co-exist with the kanto boys, the rappers, the pranksters, the firebreather, the gamers and anime character, the LGBT and the town queen.  Nothing extraordinary in a poor or lower-income community where loud music can burst into the scene anytime and even karaokes are no match to giant sound systems. The Pinoy “masa” spirit at its best; a piece of nostalgia for OFWs but a wonder or puzzle for foreigners.

Why SB19 took to this high energy and creative effort is probably because many still box them as K-pop wannabes despite baring their souls as Pinoy, charting on local and global platforms, winning awards, becoming cultural ambassadors, and defended by a dedicated fanbase that takes pride in the Pinoy language (Tagalog or Bisaya) and could outsmart even the largest fan armies around the world.

But this time they are not alone. Ultimately the pop cultural and internet icons took notice of what SB19 meant for and in the industry and, as if showing a united front, graced _Dungka!_  As SB19 tells bashers in the mv to get lost (“Tumabi ka,d’yan, do’n, do’n, kung di mo to gusto, tumabi ka d’yan”),  familiar faces come from different fields of pop culture, one after the other, joining crowds as SB19 Justin shouts with a megaphone atop a jeepney and SB19 Stell holds a red flag atop another.  And how are they getting into a counter-offensive?  By repeatedly pushing them out (d’on ka, d’on ka, di mo to kaya, di to basta-basta) and having placards with slogans like lika _Artista ng Bayan,  Sining ang Sandata sa Kulturang  Mapagpalaya,_ and _Pangalagaan ang Kultura_.

Indeed art is freedom of expression. SB19, known for mixing several genres in one music, will not settle for the ordinary or mediocre.  Reactions like “there is so much going on” in practically every record they produce has already become common to music fans and reactors.  Yet respect comes when they push boundaries coupled with hard work, passion and inspiration. _Dungka!_ is no exception. While the song is a diss track there are more layers of meaning that come in between.

Yes, guest appearances by Vice Ganda, Mimiyuuh, Maymay Entrata, Alodia Gosengfiao, Ben&Ben’s Pat and Agnes,  Ghost Wrecker, Kween Yasmin, Maliputon, Smugglaz, Shehyee, Sassa Gurl and Jayat definitely added color, hype and excitement to audiences— again giving SB19 one million views in 24 hours.

But beyond the grit and glitter, SB19 has proven that its artistry is meant not just to raise the bar of OPM or P-pop locally and globally but to also use their music, talent and skills in raising social awareness.  In this season of competing political dynasties, fake news, dishonesty and fraud., the trapos are singled out.  _Dungka!_ becomes a call to get the trapos out of people’s lives as SB19 Justin purposely covers a trapo poster with a _Sining Ang Sandata_ poster. Another scene sees a trapo unable to campaign when his path is barricaded by vehicles and a set of drums left on the street.

The bashers and the trapos have one thing in common.  They are selfishly motivated.  They want to maintain the status quo and resist change, even while the current has already begun.

Indeed _Dungka!_ is another worthy dive into the messaging of SB19.  Nothing puchu-puchu for P-pop kings who walk the talk when dreaming beyond themselves and elevating the Filipino music industry to new levels and greatness.

_(Dungka!_ is a song from SB19’s Simula at Wakas EP (extended playlist) launched last April 25 and follows the success of DAM, the EP’s carrier single.)
